The test image shows a green coffee leaf with two irregular brown lesions. One is a dark oval patch (left), one is a larger irregular brown area (right), with some white/cream material visible between them. No trail patterns, no yellow powdery lesions, no clear circular bull's-eye spots.

Top candidates: Cerscospora or Phoma (irregular dark spots; Cerscospora has no KB description so I need a visual reference).

**Analysis of test image:**
- Large irregular brown patches on the upper leaf surface
- Some white/cream material visible between lesions
- Not circular bull's-eyes (rules out Brown_Eye_Spot, Berry_Blotch)
- No yellow/orange powdery lesions (rules out Rust)
- Cerscospora reference shows smaller isolated spots — doesn't match the large blotchy patches in test image
- Remaining candidates: Miner and Phoma

**Distinguishing Miner vs Phoma:**
- Phoma: circular dark spots (test image patches are irregular, not circular)
- Miner: "irregular brown spots on the upper leaf surface" + "large necrotic patches caused by larval mining" — matches the irregular blotchy pattern; white/cream material consistent with exposed mesophyll from larval feeding

The large, irregular necrotic patches on the upper leaf surface strongly point to Miner.
